summary: A static build: Astro on the frontend, hosted on Netlify for about $0 a month; no backend or database is needed. It gives search engines full HTML pages and serves pre-built files, so there is no server for a solo developer to run.

frontend.justification: Astro is the frontend for a Content / blog / marketing (SEO) project with about 600 daily users (~0.2 requests/s at peak), built by a solo developer in 2 weeks. Search visibility is marked critical (organic traffic is the business), and it serves full HTML from the server or the build (SEO 5.0/5), so crawlers read the content without running JavaScript. It leads the runner-up, SvelteKit, by 1.1 points (out of 100 on the whole-stack score, the average of the four layer scores).

alternatives.why_not: Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 1.1 points. Astro is stronger on low ops burden (5.0 vs 4.0), team skill match (4.0 vs 3.5); SvelteKit is stronger on rich client interactivity (5.0 vs 2.0), hiring pool (3.0 vs 2.0).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 12.0 points. Astro is stronger on performance / latency (5.0 vs 4.0); Server-rendered HTML + HTMX is stronger on learning curve (5.0 vs 4.0), team skill match (4.5 vs 4.0). A stack compatibility rule costs it 13.0 points, more than the whole gap, while on this layer's own criteria it is 1.0 points ahead: HTMX needs a server that renders HTML; BaaS/function backends return JSON, and a static site runs no server code at all.

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 2.7 points. supporting.choice: An uptime check plus the host's web analytics
supporting.justification: With no server code there is nothing to trace; watch that the pages are up and how fast they load. A 99% availability target (requirements.availability) allows about 432 minutes of downtime a month, so failures must show within minutes.

alternatives.why_not: They show the app is down, not why
Without traces and metrics there is no way to see which call is slow or failing

tradeoffs: Telemetry volume is billed: sample traces and set log retention
